02 / NGOs · Donors · Programme teams

The Costing Clinic

Pilot

Pressure-test the numbers.

A focused review of one programme’s costing or financing model, with an assurance memo and correction roadmap. Scope and timing agreed together.

Discuss the pilot↗

A short, senior review for a programme team that needs to know whether its numbers can carry the decision.

Who it is for

Programme teams, NGOs, donors and delivery partners with an active costing, budget or financing model.

What the pilot includes

  • Pre-read and scoping call against the decision, deadline and available evidence.
  • Structured review of cost drivers, funding logic, assumptions and sensitivity points.
  • A concise assurance memo: what holds, what needs correction and what remains uncertain.
  • A practical correction roadmap, sequenced around the next decision or submission.

What it does not include

  • A full feasibility study, audit or donor certification.
  • A guarantee of approval, funding or procurement success.

Pilot status: scope, fee and turnaround are agreed case by case while the format is being tested with early users.

03 / Regional & multi-country programmes

Toolkit Licensing

Pilot

Give good analysis a repeatable form.

Exploring reusable costing frameworks, training and an expert assurance layer. Availability and licensing terms are being developed.

Discuss the pilot↗

Turn a proven costing approach into a repeatable internal capability for a team, programme or region.

Who it is for

Regional programmes, consulting firms, NGOs, universities and delivery partners that need a consistent costing language across contexts.

What the pilot includes

  • A scoped toolkit: templates, guidance notes, worked examples and assumptions register.
  • An onboarding session for the people who will use and adapt it.
  • Optional expert assurance review for the first live application.
  • A maintenance conversation covering versioning, permissions and responsible reuse.

What it does not include

  • A licence to donor-owned or third-party deliverables without confirmed rights.
  • A universal model that removes the need for local data, judgement or adaptation.

Pilot status: the toolkit format, support model and licensing terms are being developed with selected partners; no catalogue or standard price is published yet.

Any future licence will cover only material with confirmed rights and permissions. No donor-owned deliverables are offered for sale.
